statements.quote: All sites performed the same test protocol – with the exceptions marked below. Before the experimental tasks, the participants had a 30 min presentation of TRIZ and a 15 min of prompt engineering. They also completed a short practice problem to familiarize themselves with the procedure (TRIZ steps, and LLM use). The practice task was distinct from the test problems and not included in the analysis.

statements.quote: The students using the TRIZ-C+LLM method were given a prompt-pack with concrete prompt instructions and examples for 1) problem framing (clarify the challenge), 2) TRIZ contradiction parameters identification, 3) relevant TRIZ inventive principles suggestions, 4) solution generation and 5) diversity check.

notes:
Read the complete 334-line markdown conversion, including the acknowledgements and references, and checked the PDF text and all PDF link annotations. The saved version of record has 10 pages (printed pp. 507-516) and no appendix or embedded file (PyMuPDF embfile_count=0). The on-request statement was checked directly on PDF p. 9. No code-availability statement, preregistration, study-data repository URL, or supplementary-file reference was found. Statements also record the descriptions of the questionnaire, practice material and prompt pack; their mention does not establish public access to the original files. For two quotations, the publisher full text confirms TRIZ-C+LLM where the PDF text extraction yields U+0001 and the markdown yields U+FFFD or loses a hyphen; no wording was inferred.

forms/c101.json identifies one randomized study, S1. Its data_and_code.data_url is prose saying the data are available from the corresponding author upon reasonable request, not a URL; code_url is empty. The paper's on-request statement applies to the data and materials used/analyzed, but the exact contents and format of anything an author might provide are unconfirmed. No author was contacted and no access was requested.

Publisher check: https://doi.org/10.1017/pds.2026.10409 returned HTTP 200 after redirecting to https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/proceedings-of-the-design-society/article/evaluating-triz-with-and-without-llm-support-an-experimental-study-on-engineering-problemsolving/09B3955101E1013E73E8EB6C528DAE56. A direct request to the landing page also returned HTTP 200. It contains the article full text and the same data-availability statement, and its article metadata explicitly says supplementaryMaterials:[]. No article-specific supplementary data files were listed. The article is not counted as a data deposit; its publicly printed aggregate results are not participant records.

The only nonbibliographic external material URL in the paper, https://www.triz40.com/, returned HTTP 200 and redirected to https://www.triz40.com/TRIZ_GB.php. It is the general TRIZ contradiction-matrix website used by the control group, not a deposit of this experiment's assignments, scores, outputs, prompt pack or questionnaire responses, and is not counted in deposits. The mailto link was not followed. The publisher's generic navigation links about submitting supplementary material are not files for this article.

Full-title and exact first-author searches found zero matches at all four requested repository APIs once the two initial Zenodo validation errors were corrected. Zenodo initially returned HTTP 400 because anonymous searches permit size <= 25, not size=100; the same queries with size=25 returned HTTP 200 and zero results. Shortened title searches and name variants are recorded separately. OSF's requested endpoint filters node titles, so the first-author queries search that name in titles, not the full contributor database; this limits author-based coverage.

The broad OSF title-substring search TRIZ returned 100 nodes (API-reported total 100, next=null); titles were examined and the descriptions of the four nodes actually naming TRIZ were inspected. They concern Unified Metrology-TRIZ Neural Machine Translation (swcy8, d2w3h, jw6et) or Fresh Flower Product-Service Systems Designed with TRIZ Based Method (hxj6r), rather than this randomized engineering-student experiment. The other hits include unrelated words such as 'matriz' and 'diretrizes'. The Cok title-substring search returned 74 unrelated nodes, with no matching study. These searches were requested again with compact output to inspect the returned metadata without console truncation; counts were unchanged. These unrelated nodes are not counted as deposits of c101 and were not treated as participant-data candidates.

The broad Zenodo query Vanja AND (Čok OR Cok) initially exceeded a local 8 MiB response cap and could not be parsed; that failed attempt has n_results=null and its HTTP status was not retained by the exception handler. A size=1 request parsed successfully (HTTP 200) and reported 13 results. The first record was an ESPnet2 pretrained speech-recognition model by Pavel Denisov (10.5281/zenodo.7374729), not this paper or author. To classify all 13 without downloading the very large irrelevant metadata pages, the same query restricted to title:"ESPnet2 pretrained model" returned 13, and excluding that title returned zero, both HTTP 200. Thus all 13 broad-name hits belonged to this unrelated model-title family. The exact surname-first variants also returned zero. No relevant deposit was found. No files were downloaded to disk, and no participant-data file or observed columns/rows were available to inspect.

The public source cannot supply the separate C3 innovativeness scores needed for the novelty record in final.open_items, nor establish whether the excluded GT student had been randomized or to which arm. No public participant/output records were found from which to calculate per-person scores, arm means/SDs/SEs, independently checked analyzed counts, or text/idea diversity. Table 2 already reports rounded aggregate design-quality summaries; those do not establish access to individual scores or texts. The randomization procedure also remains unreported. what_we_could_compute is null because no usable public dataset was confirmed. Confidence is high in the on_request classification, which is stated directly by the paper and publisher; repository searches do not prove that no unindexed or differently titled deposit exists.

Every distinct bibliographic HTTPS link in the PDF was also requested with urllib and User-Agent atlas-screening/0.1. These are citations to other works, not c101 data deposits; HTTP 403 responses were not bypassed.
